title: A Close Approximation
statement: Consider all fractions $\frac{p}{q}$ with $p$ and $q$ positive integers, $q \le 200$ and $\frac{p}{q} \ne \frac{7}{19}$. Among the values of these fractions, exactly one is closest to $\frac{7}{19}$. Write this value as $\frac{a}{b}$ in lowest terms, with $a$ and $b$ positive integers. Find $a+b$.
hints: Put $\frac{p}{q} - \frac{7}{19}$ over a common denominator. Look at what values the numerator can take and how the size of $q$ affects the difference.

The difference has size $\frac{|19p-7q|}{19q}$, where the numerator is a positive integer. Use modular arithmetic: reduce modulo $19$ to find which $q$ allow the numerator to equal $1$. The inverse of $7$ modulo $19$ will help.

Since $7 \cdot 11 \equiv 1 \pmod{19}$, a numerator of $1$ requires $q \equiv 8$ or $11 \pmod{19}$. Find the largest such $q \le 200$ and its $p$. A numerator of at least $2$ gives a distance of at least $\frac{2}{19 \cdot 200}$, so compare this with what you found.
solution: For a fraction $\frac{p}{q}$ we have $$\left|\dfrac{p}{q} - \dfrac{7}{19}\right| = \dfrac{|19p - 7q|}{19q}.$$ Let $N = |19p - 7q|$. This is an integer, and it is not $0$ because $\frac{p}{q} \ne \frac{7}{19}$, so $N \ge 1$. A small distance needs a small $N$ and a large $q$. First we find which $q$ allow $N = 1$. This means $19p - 7q = 1$ or $19p - 7q = -1$, so $7q \equiv -1$ or $7q \equiv 1 \pmod{19}$. Since $7 \cdot 11 = 77 = 4 \cdot 19 + 1$, multiplying a congruence by $11$ undoes multiplication by $7$ modulo $19$. Hence $7q \equiv -1$ gives $q \equiv -11 \equiv 8 \pmod{19}$, and $7q \equiv 1$ gives $q \equiv 11 \pmod{19}$. The largest $q \le 200$ with $q \equiv 8 \pmod{19}$ is $198 = 10 \cdot 19 + 8$. The largest $q \le 200$ with $q \equiv 11 \pmod{19}$ is $182 = 9 \cdot 19 + 11$, because the next one is $201$. So $N = 1$ forces $q \le 198$. For $q = 198$ we need $19p - 7 \cdot 198 = 1$, that is $19p = 1387$, so $p = 73$. This fraction has distance $\frac{1}{19 \cdot 198}$. Now we compare this with every other fraction, in two cases. If $N = 1$ and $q < 198$, the distance is $\frac{1}{19q} > \frac{1}{19 \cdot 198}$. If $N \ge 2$, then since $q \le 200$ the distance is at least $\frac{2}{19 \cdot 200} = \frac{1}{19 \cdot 100} > \frac{1}{19 \cdot 198}$. If $N = 1$ and $q = 198$, then $q \equiv 8 \pmod{19}$ forces $19p - 7q = 1$, so $p = 73$ and this is the fraction already found. So $\frac{73}{198}$ is the unique closest value. This fraction is in lowest terms, because any common divisor of $73$ and $198$ divides $19 \cdot 73 - 7 \cdot 198 = 1$. Therefore $a = 73$ and $b = 198$, and $a + b = \mathbf{271}$. Why this works. modular-inverse, bounding, modular-arithmetic: the inverse of $7$ modulo $19$ identifies the denominators giving the smallest possible numerator, and a size bound shows that no larger numerator can compete.
